name: FedCM (Federated Credential Management)
plain: Lets a site ask the browser to sign the person in with Google, Apple or similar without third party cookies.
meaning: Gives the site an ID token for a chosen identity provider account; the browser mediates the prompt.

access.prompt_ui: Browser account chooser (passive in the page or active after a click)
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Lets a site ask the browser to sign the person in with Google, Apple or similar without third party cookies.

fields.name: accounts
fields.precision: only shown in the browser UI

limits.headline: Can sign you in with Google, Apple or similar using a browser account picker
limits.user_action: You tap Sign in with Google (or similar) or answer a prompt that appears on the page
can: Show a browser box listing accounts you have with a sign in provider
Receive a sign in token for the account you choose
Show the prompt on the page itself or after you tap a button
cannot: Get your account details before you approve
Use third party cookies to track you quietly between sites
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support it. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: A browser run login box that signs you in with Google, Apple or similar, with no cookie tricks.

marketing.name: Federated Credential Management
marketing.pitch: Chrome pitches it as keeping one click sign in alive as third party cookies fade, with the browser running the prompt.

marketing.name: FedCM API
marketing.pitch: Describes a browser mediated way for people to sign in to sites using an identity provider, without tracking by cookies or redirects.

story.for_you: You see a small prompt from the browser offering to continue as your account. You tap to agree. Nothing happens until you do.
story.for_makers: Makers keep one tap social login working as third party cookies go away. Sign in conversion stays high and the browser enforces privacy rules for them.

use_cases.example: A web game portal shows a prompt so a player signs in and loads a saved profile at once.
A streaming site offers one tap sign in so a viewer resumes where they stopped.
A store shows the prompt on page load so returning customers reach saved carts faster.
A news site uses it to recognize subscribers and skip the paywall.
A web app embeds the prompt in a sidebar so teammates can join a shared document fast.
Ad and measurement partners lose the old hidden login cookie link, so a visit can no longer be quietly matched to a Google account.

risks: Identity provider may see your visits

technical_bounds: Chrome and Edge only; Firefox and Safari not shipped (Firefox ships Login Status 138)
IdP Registration, Fields API and multiple IdPs still on the roadmap
Safari 27 has options members but no IdentityCredential

abuse: IdP learns which RP the person visits

history.change: Structured JSON token accepted, stricter client metadata checks
accounts_endpoint enforced, IdentityCredentialError.code renamed to error
